newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees 96/97 world cereals trade 186 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees 96/97 world cereals trade 186 mln tonnes.

text.p: World trade in cereals in 1996/97 is forecast at 186 million tonnes, down nearly 15 million tonnes or seven percent from 1995/96 levels, the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Thursday.

"The bulk of this year's contraction in world trade is in wheat and coarse grains, but preliminary indications also point to a slight decrease in rice imports," it said in its latest Food Outlook report.
It said world trade in wheat and wheat flour in 1996/97 (July/June) was forecast at only 85 million tonnes, some six million below the revised estimate for 1995/96.

"Larger plantings, due to high prices combined with generally favourable weather, particularly among the importing countries, are expected to result in the smallest volume of wheat trade in a decade," the Rome-based agency said.
It said aggregate wheat imports by developing countries in 1996/97 was forecast at 69 million tonnes, nearly four million less than last year.
"Among the developing countries, imports are forecast to fall most significantly in China," FAO said, due to a bumper wheat crop this year and slow purchases during the early months of the season.
